item.title: BraveDebloater: A Cross-Platform PowerShell Script for Brave Browser Customization
item.description:
BraveDebloater: A Cross-Platform PowerShell Script for Brave Browser Customization

BraveDebloater is a new PowerShell-based tool designed to remove specific features and extras from Brave Browser using enterprise policies. The script is not affiliated with or endorsed by Brave Software. It operates on Windows, macOS, and Linux, writing native configuration files for each platform to disable chosen components while maintaining full transparency.

🧩 How It Works

The tool is built on PowerShell, which serves as the cross-platform runtime. When executed, it writes configuration files native to the operating system:

  • Windows: Registry policies
  • macOS: Defaults or plist payloads
  • Linux: JSON policy files

The script starts in preview mode, meaning no changes are made until the user explicitly adds the -Apply flag. Before an apply run, the tool writes a backup unless the user specifies -NoBackup for policy-only changes. This backup can be restored using the -UndoFromBackup command.

⚙️ Supported Features

Users can select specific features to disable via the command-line interface. The tool supports the following Brave-specific surfaces and telemetry options:

Feature Area Example Commands/Policy Names
Rewards BraveRewardsDisabled
Wallet BraveWalletDisabled
VPN BraveVPNDisabled
Leo AI Chat BraveAIChatEnabled
News BraveNewsDisabled
Talk BraveTalkDisabled
Playlist BravePlaylistEnabled
Email Aliases EmailAliasesEnabled
Telemetry BraveP3AEnabled, BraveStatsPingEnabled, BraveWebDiscoveryEnabled
Chromium Metrics metrics_reports_enabled

An “Extreme” preset can additionally disable background mode, promotions, Browser Labs, new tab cards, shopping list, QR generator, translate prompts, autofill, and the Google search side panel. Optional profile preference cleanup can hide new tab, sponsored background, and toolbar surfaces by editing per-profile Preferences JSON; this step requires closing Brave before applying. DNS-over-HTTPS mode can also be configured via the -DnsOverHttps flag.

🛡️ Safety and Limitations

The tool is designed with strict safety boundaries:

  • No Update Disabling: It does not disable Brave updates, as update policies are on the blocklist.
  • Shields Protection: It does not turn off Brave Shields, add allowlists, or weaken Safe Browsing. An optional -LockShields add-on can only enforce stricter Shields defaults.
  • No Binary Patching: It does not edit hosts files, remove extensions, patch binaries, or install anything into Brave.
  • Transparency: It does not run hidden. All set policies are listed in brave://policy with their values. The -Doctor flag reports the current state in read-only mode.

🚀 Usage

To use BraveDebloater, users pick features and copy the matching command from bravedebloater.tersa.tech. Each command previews first. To write the policy, the user adds -Apply and then restarts Brave. To undo changes, users follow the preview and apply commands provided in the Restore section.

#BraveBrowser #PowerShell #CrossPlatform #BrowserCustomization #OpenSourceTools

Source: osfv/BraveDebloater

item.title: Slurm 26.11 Introduces HRES to Enable Native Quantum Processor Scheduling
item.description:
Slurm 26.11 Introduces HRES to Enable Native Quantum Processor Scheduling

Slurm 26.11 adds Hierarchical Resources (HRES) plugins that enable quantum processing units (QPUs) to be scheduled as native cluster resources, allowing HPC centers to integrate quantum accelerators alongside traditional supercomputing systems.

🔍 Overview

National programs across North America, Europe, and Asia are integrating quantum processing units (QPUs) into supercomputing centers worldwide. These QPUs operate as cluster-wide accelerators, distinct from node-attached GPUs.

🧩 How it works

The HRES plugin interface uses short, portable Lua scripts to manage QPU scheduling:

  • Reports device health to the scheduler
  • Accepts device options as part of resource requests
  • Runs setup and teardown code at each job stage
  • Describes QPUs to HPC software via QRMI and QDMI open source efforts

⚙️ Key details

The architecture differs fundamentally from GPU scheduling:

Feature GRES (GPUs) HRES (QPUs)
Scope Per compute node Cluster-wide
Management Built into Slurm Plugin-based
Access Jobs on specific node Jobs on allowed nodes

A QPU is modeled using a single layer in resources.yaml covering nodes that can reach the device, with a count of one. The plugin logic is separate from site configuration, allowing vendors to distribute it across installations.

🚀 Availability

HRES entered Slurm in version 25.05 as a beta feature and reached production maturity in version 26.11, representing an evolution of the licensing mechanism with similar counting semantics but node-specific associations.

#Slurm #QuantumComputing #HPC #Supercomputing #QPU #Scheduling

Source: Integrating QPUs into Supercomputing Centers Using Slurm HRES Plugins | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: NVIDIA releases gds-diag tool to simplify GPUDirect Storage diagnostics
item.description:
NVIDIA releases gds-diag tool to simplify GPUDirect Storage diagnostics

NVIDIA has introduced gds‑diag, an open‑source command‑line utility (with an optional AI‑agent skill) that assesses environments, identifies problems, and suggests improvements for GPUDirect Storage deployments.

🔍 Overview

  • GPUDirect Storage (GDS) accelerates GPU storage access in on‑premises and cloud environments.
  • It provides a robust, portable, and efficient data path between NVIDIA GPUs and storage targets to increase bandwidth, minimize latency, and reduce CPU and memory utilization across a broad range of platforms, application frameworks, and workload patterns.
  • Configuring GDS starts with understanding your environment – which settings and storage paths are appropriate for your platform and workload?

🛠️ How gds‑diag works

  • Command‑line mode – a single Python script with multiple subcommands that focus on different diagnostic tasks.
  • AI‑agent mode – a natural‑language interface that interprets intent, selects and invokes the appropriate subcommands, and coordinates multi‑step diagnostic workflows.
  • The agent skill adds model‑guided reasoning: it can interpret diagnostic results, apply relevant system context, and propose or carry out appropriate remediation.
  • The tool runs on Linux systems with Python 3.8 or newer. NVIDIA datacenter‑class GPU and CUDA Toolkit 12.2 or newer are required for GDS itself, but they are not dependencies of gds‑diag.

🚀 Getting Started

  1. Clone the repository: git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/MagnumIO.git
  2. Choose a usage model:
    • Command‑line tool – deterministic, minimal‑dependency path.
    • AI agent – intuitive, flexible, natural‑language interaction (recommended when available).
  3. Open the gds-diag directory in your preferred AI coding assistant and follow the Agent skill usage guidance (if using the agent mode).
  4. Run ./gds-diag.py --help to browse subcommands, or run ./gds-diag.py all /path/to/check for an end‑to‑end diagnostic sequence.

📋 Diagnostic command categories

Category Example subcommand Purpose
End‑to‑end checks all Automatically selects appropriate diagnostics for your environment and runs them in sequence.
Preparing for installation pre-install Checks GPU support and CUDA Toolkit installation.
Storage planning support-matrix Views supported storage targets and helps plan your deployment.

The tool works in bare‑metal, virtual‑machine, and container environments.

📦 Availability

  • gds‑diag is bundled with the NVIDIA Magnum IO GitHub repository and has no additional dependencies to install.
  • It is validated with both Claude and Codex, and may work with other AI tools as well.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a robust, portable, and efficient data path for GPU‑centric workloads.
  • Reduces CPU and memory utilization while increasing bandwidth and lowering latency.
  • Offers both a deterministic command‑line experience and a flexible natural‑language agent, giving users multiple ways to optimize GDS deployments.

#NVIDIA #GPUDirectStorage #AIagents #Linux #Diagnostics

Source: How to Check and Configure NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage for Your Platform | NVIDIA Technical Blog
